title: Atlas FieldOps — acquisition decision
decision_question: Should Atlas FieldOps buy the scheduling software company RouteSprout in 2027, and on what terms, rather than build or partner?

initial_hypothesis.statement: Acquire RouteSprout for $18M upfront and complete integration in six months; $2.4M cross-sell ARR justifies it.
initial_hypothesis.explanation: Full cash purchase is infeasible under $9M floor; staged or partnered acquisition may be defensible only after ARR, churn, synergy and future-earnout diligence.

key_insights.text: Full deal requires $22.00M immediately and leaves $2.00M, violating $9M minimum cash.
Headline valuation is 3.75× verified ARR, not 2.5×; the seller uses $7.2M bookings including one-off pilots.
Base cross-sell ARR contributes $1.07M annually net of 80% GM and $0.85M additional support; stress case $-0.21M.
Customer churn 21% and six-month integration assumptions make the seller synergy case uncertain.
Staged cash expenditure $14.50M just passes the initial cash floor with $9.50M left, but its contingent $7M earnout is a future cash risk.
A nonexclusive partnership can test demand while preserving cash, but price, exclusivity and renewal exposure need negotiation.

decision_relevant_evidence.text: Board $9M minimum cash and $15M spendable limit
Churn, renewal cohorts and integration cost exposure

contradictory_evidence: Sellers multiple uses bookings, finance uses ARR
Large accounts renew more but also receive more support
Bookings include nonrenewable pilots and multi-year face value

reasoning_traps.text: Treating $2.4M cross-sell ARR as immediate cash EBITDA
Ignoring earnout or integration costs in minimum cash tests

key_tradeoffs.text: Speed to feature vs capital preservation
Acquisition control vs retention and integration risk

plausible_recommendations.text: Start nonexclusive commercial partnership while negotiating an evidence- and cash-gated acquisition option.
Pursue staged purchase only if independently verified ARR, retention, integration scope and earnout reserve support it.
Buy for $18M cash plus $4M integration under current limits.

defensibility_criteria: Cash floor governs the full and staged alternatives
Valuation uses recurring ARR not gross bookings
Synergies are translated to cash contribution with uncertainty
Tradeoffs between buy, partner and build are made explicit

decision_requirements.question: Can the initial and future cash commitments satisfy minimum liquidity?
Is the strongest non-acquisition path weighed?
